title: get_dataframe decodes every pre-118 .dta as Latin-1; cp1252 files (EHCVM-1 2018-19 s01_me_*) serve C1 controls for oe/euro/quotes -- 1,501 C1-signature labels corpus-wide
priority_why: Served text carries C1 controls in several live tables (Serbia and Montenegro sample.strata 1,661 rows / cluster_features.Region 162; Mali food_acquired.j 4,447; BF 2014 j 45,738 of which the 0x85/0x9C class is this bug), but it is label corruption, not a wrong number, and the cohort crosswalks are keyed on the damage so a reader change can silently un-match 278,777+ rows.
summary: Claim holds on today's development. get_dataframe -> read_file (local_tools.py:1308-1310) -> ligonlibrary.from_dta -> pandas StataReader, with no encoding ever passed from the YAML path (country.py:1453 df_data_grabber call carries no encoding=) and pandas picking latin-1 for format<118 by rule. The installed ligonlibrary (dist-info 0.2.2, RECORD hash matches the file) now has a strict _coerce_label, but for str labels it PINS the encode leg to latin-1 and decodes UTF-8 -- so even if encoding='cp1252' were plumbed, a cp1252 C1 label would still be returned unchanged (the round-trip fails and the value is returned as-is). Option B of the issue (per-file encoding: declaration) therefore needs new plumbing in BOTH grab_data and the decoder, not just a YAML key. Sizing from slurm_logs/dta_encoding/sweep_38595301.jsonl.gz: 136 files / 1,501 C1 labels; 64 of those files / 831 labels are DECLARED by some table; 61 files / 827 labels are format<118 (the issue's scope). By country: Cambodia 649, Niger 307, Uganda 213, Burkina_Faso 130, Albania 38, Mali 29, Senegal 29, Benin 21, Serbia and Montenegro 15. Warm-cache scan of all 400 var/*.parquet (served pre-finalize values; $STAGE/served_mojibake_scan.txt): C1/mojibake reaches Serbia and Montenegro sample.strata (1,661 rows, '\x8aumadija' = cp1252 S-caron) and cluster_features.Region (162), Mali food_acquired.j 2018-19 (4,447: 'Viande de b\x9cuf' 3,453 + '\x8cufs' 994), Burkina_Faso food_acquired.j (45,738 in 2014 + 1,399 in 2018-19), Uganda shocks.HowCoped* (0x85 ellipsis, cosmetic), GhanaLSS nonfood_expenditures.j / community_prices.j (#926 class, NOT this bug -- those files are format 118). Senegal food_acquired.u shows 41,347 raw mojibake rows in the parquet but every one matches a u-crosswalk key (measured), so the API serves them clean -- the load-bearing pairing CONTENTS.org describes. The four _decode_cp1252 helpers (Benin/2018-19, Niger/2018-19, Senegal/2018-19, Togo/2018 _/mapping.py) exist and apply to Relationship only. THIRD CLASS, outside the issue's format<118 scoping: cp1252 bytes inside a UTF-8-declared (format 117/118) file, which pandas decodes through its per-string latin-1 FALLBACK -- and on pandas 3.0.6 it does so SILENTLY: pd.read_stata on GhanaLSS/2016-17/Data/g7sec9a.dta raised no UnicodeWarning yet 390,140 of 7,077,839 s9aname values carry a C1 control. The sweep counts 17 C1 value labels in format-118 files (GhanaSPS 01fi_generaleducation, Burkina_Faso s07b_me_bfa2018, Ethiopia sect3_hh_w4) and never probed str columns, so the issue's format<118 scoping undercounts. Why Senegal's 41,347 parquet rows are clean at the API while Mali's 4,447 are not: Senegal's u is mapped at READ time (bare u: s07bq03b plus a country table named u, matched by _apply_categorical_mappings), so the parquet holds raw values by design; Mali's j is mapped at BUILD time (Mali/2018-19/_/data_info.yml:196 mappings: ['harmonize_food','Code','Preferred Label']), so a C1 value surviving in the parquet means the key did not match -- the same failure as BF rows 303/304.
evidence: lsms_library/local_tools.py:1308-1310 (from_dta attempt, no encoding on the YAML path); lsms_library/country.py:1453 (df_data_grabber call passes no encoding); .venv/.../ligonlibrary/dataframes.py _coerce_label (encode leg pinned to latin-1, decode utf-8, unchanged on failure); python over slurm_logs/dta_encoding/sweep_38595301.jsonl.gz (c1 by country/format/declared); pyarrow scan of /global/scratch/.../cache/lsms_library/*/var/*.parquet for [\x80-\x9f]|Ã|Å|Â -> $STAGE/served_mojibake_scan.txt; Senegal u keys: df_from_orgfile(Senegal/_/categorical_mapping.org,'u') vs parquet u (41,347/41,347 match); grep -ln _decode_cp1252 countries/*/*/_/mapping.py -> Benin, Senegal, Togo, Niger. pd.read_stata(g7sec9a blob, convert_categoricals=False) under warnings.catch_warnings(record=True): [] warnings, s9aname 390,140/7,077,839 rows with [\x80-\x9f]; sweep 'by format': 118 -> 17 C1 labels; Mali/2018-19/_/data_info.yml:196.
approach: Reader-level, option A: in get_dataframe's Stata branch (or a thin wrapper around from_dta) re-decode value labels AND str columns with the predicate the four _decode_cp1252 helpers already use -- a codepoint in U+0080-U+009F -> value.encode('latin-1').decode('cp1252'), falling back to latin-1 for the five cp1252 holes -- with NO format gate: legitimate text never carries a C1 control, and gating on format<118 would skip the format-118 fallback class measured above (GhanaLSS g7sec9a str column, GhanaSPS/BF/Ethiopia value labels). Retire the four wave helpers in the same PR. Not the double-encoded (Ã/Â) class, which is #794's strategy-B cohort and is untouched by this change.

If the fix lands in ligonlibrary instead, NO fingerprint moves (external package source is not hashed) and warm parquets keep serving C1 graded fresh -- a manual LSMS_CACHE_SCHEMA bump is then mandatory. title: UnicodeWarning in from_dta: the warning is benign; the silent latin-1 path beside it is where the risk lives (and Senegal's mojibake is load-bearing)
priority_why: One live served defect (Burkina Faso food_acquired.j, now 47,137 rows after #851 un-deleted the 2014 p2-p4 rows) fragments the harmonization axis three ways; the rest is latent (crosswalks keyed on damage) or already fixed upstream.
summary: Partial. The UPSTREAM half (§D items 1-3) is resolved: the installed ligonlibrary _coerce_label no longer uses errors='ignore', returns a value unchanged when the latin-1->utf-8 round trip fails (which is the format-118 guard the issue asked for: 'Boîte de tomate' survives), and its docstring now says what encoding= actually does. Verified on the venv's ligonlibrary 0.2.2 (dist-info RECORD hash matches dataframes.py) -- but pyproject/poetry.lock pin >=0.2.3, so the fix was verified on a version the lock does not name; confirm 0.2.3 carries it. The IN-REPO half is open and has moved: (1) the live BF leak the comments found (12,933 rows) is now 47,137 rows in the warm cache -- 2014 'Cube (Maggi, Jumbo,\x85)' 38,982 + 'Viandes de b\x9cufs fraîches' 6,756, 2018-19 'Viande de bÅ\x93uf' 1,399 -- because #851 (1446e4c1b) stopped deleting the 2014 p2-p4 passages, so the leak scaled with the row count; (2) Mali food_acquired.j 2018-19 serves 4,447 C1 rows from the same class (not in the issue); (3) the three dead encoding=-passing wave scripts are still on disk (Senegal/2018-19, Burkina_Faso/2018-19, Burkina_Faso/2021-22 _/food_acquired.py); (4) the strategy-B cohort migration (Benin/BF/Senegal/Togo onto _decode_mojibake + crosswalk re-key, ~278,777+ rows) has not happened and nothing marks which country is which; (5) Senegal's u pairing still holds: 41,347 raw mojibake u rows in the parquet, 41,347 match a crosswalk key. Mali vs Senegal asymmetry: Mali's j is mapped at build time (Mali/2018-19/_/data_info.yml:196 harmonize_food on Code), so a C1 value in the parquet is a key that did NOT match, exactly like BF rows 303/304; Senegal's u is mapped at read time (country table named u), so its raw parquet values are expected. OPEN for the diagnose step: Mali/_/categorical_mapping.org:362 appears to hold the same U+009C bytes as the served 'Viande de b\x9cuf' yet does not match -- whether the warm parquet predates the org edit, df_from_orgfile normalises the key, or the Code column is read differently is unmeasured.

title: GhanaLSS nonfood_expenditures serves 25,585 rows with cp1252-as-Latin1 C1 controls in j; the bad code points are committed in curated config, so the #805 reader fix will not clear them
priority_why: Served labels are visibly wrong (U+0092/0096/0094 in 27 j labels, 25,585 rows of nonfood_expenditures plus 927 rows of community_prices j/Description), and a sweep found it is the only country where C1 sits in a SERVED Preferred Label column rather than a key; no number is wrong.
summary: Claim holds: warm GhanaLSS/var/nonfood_expenditures.parquet has 25,585 rows / 27 distinct j with C1 controls, all 2016-17; the country org file has 28 C1 cells (nonfood_items Preferred Label + Label_2016-17), and GhanaLSS/2016-17/_/categorical_mapping.org has 3 more in harmonize_price_item (lines 915/932/954) which reach community_prices.j AND .Description (927 rows each, 2016-17) -- an instance the issue did not count. PR #949 (merged 2026-09-18) explicitly 'reported, not touched' #926 and listed the other countries' C1 cells. The MECHANISM is slightly different from the issue's: g7sec9a.dta is format 118 (<stata_dta> header), i.e. UTF-8-declared, and its STRING DATA carries raw cp1252 bytes -- 41,803 'Women\x92s' beside 97,531 clean "Women's" in the same file -- so pandas' per-string latin-1 FALLBACK (not the pre-118 default rule) produced U+0092 -- measured: pd.read_stata on the blob raises NO UnicodeWarning on pandas 3.0.6 and 390,140 of 7,077,839 s9aname values carry a C1 control. Consequence: #805's 'cp1252-first for format<118' would not repair a re-derivation of this crosswalk either; the fix is the config repair the issue asks for. Corpus sweep answer to the issue's last paragraph: C1 in curated org config also exists in Mali/_/categorical_mapping.org harmonize_food Code (rows 362/374), Niger/_/categorical_mapping.org harmonize_food Original Label (rows 921/922), Burkina_Faso harmonize_food Original Label (296/303/304) -- all KEY columns (load-bearing, #794's strategy B), and Uganda/_/categorical_mapping.org u table wave-label columns (325-329; u is keyed on Code, so inert). GhanaLSS is the only served-Preferred-Label instance. community_prices.j and .Description are both built from the org table (community_prices.py:65-69 code.map(items['Preferred Label']) / items['Label']), so the 927-row instance is config-side too, not a read-time artefact.
evidence: pyarrow read of GhanaLSS/var/nonfood_expenditures.parquet (25,585 rows, 27 distinct, t=2016-17); $STAGE/served_mojibake_scan.txt (community_prices j/Description 927); grep -c -P '[\x{0080}-\x{009F}]' on GhanaLSS/_/categorical_mapping.org (28) and 2016-17/_/categorical_mapping.org (3); raw blob of GhanaLSS/2016-17/Data/g7sec9a.dta: header b'<stata_dta>', count(b'Women\x92s')=41,803, count(b"Women's")=97,531; GhanaLSS/2016-17/_/nonfood_expenditures.py:99 decodes codes through nonfood_items Preferred Label; gh pr view 949 body §'GH #926 -- reported, not touched'.
approach: Config repair, one PR: in lsms_library/countries/GhanaLSS/_/categorical_mapping.org replace U+0092 -> "'", U+0096 -> '-', U+0094 -> '"' in the 28 nonfood_items cells (Preferred Label and Label_2016-17 consistently, keeping Preferred Labels injective -- the script asserts it at nonfood_expenditures.py:108), and the 3 harmonize_price_item cells in GhanaLSS/2016-17/_/categorical_mapping.org. Add a test that no curated .org under countries/ or categorical_mapping/ carries a codepoint in U+0080-U+009F (fails today on GhanaLSS, Mali, Niger, Burkina_Faso, Uganda -- so either scope it to Preferred Label columns or land the other re-keys with #794/#805). Record the mixed-encoding-in-one-file fact in GhanaLSS/_/CONTENTS.org.
verify: Cold build of GhanaLSS nonfood_expenditures and community_prices in a private root; assert 0 j values match [\x80-\x9f]; row counts unchanged (977,193 / 660,168); tests/test_ghanalss_* pass. CACHE COST: _/categorical_mapping.org is a build-time *.org input in every GhanaLSS table's hash (CLAUDE.md v0.8.0 staleness list) -> full GhanaLSS re-warm (its food_acquired alone is a 167 s warm read; cold is minutes), no other country.

title: get_dataframe's Stata attempt catches only (ValueError, struct.error) -- a CSV whose leading bytes look like a Stata header dies with an uncaught KeyError
priority_why: Content-dependent hard failure of the sanctioned reader on an ordinary CSV, reproduced today as an uncaught MemoryError; corpus exposure measured at 0 of 93 cached CSV blobs (320 unfetched, unknown), so it bites fixtures and user CSVs rather than served tables.
summary: Claim holds in substance, with a different exception on today's stack. local_tools.py:1308-1310 still wraps the from_dta attempt in except (ValueError, struct.error) (line 1310 last touched 2026-03-29, 80359af1c; PR #965 Windows readers did not change it). On pandas 3.0.6 the TYPE_MAP KeyError the issue saw is now wrapped by pandas into ValueError('cannot convert stata types'), so that exact path is closed -- but the class is not: a plain CSV with header 'hhid,name,val' and 100,000 rows escapes get_dataframe as an uncaught MemoryError raised from pandas/io/stata.py:1698 (reader.read allocating nobs x nvar from a garbage header) via ligonlibrary/dataframes.py:455 and local_tools.py:1309. 'id,...' and 'region,...' headers of the same size read fine -- content-dependent exactly as described. Sweep of the held corpus: 413 .csv/.CSV sidecars, 93 blobs present in the shared dvc-cache, 0 begin with a byte in {104,105,108,110,111,113,114,115}; 320 blobs not present and not measured.
evidence: lsms_library/local_tools.py:1308-1310; git blame -L1309,1310; repro: $STAGE/tmp/hhid_100000.csv -> MemoryError traceback (local_tools.py:1358 get_dataframe -> :1309 read_file -> ligonlibrary/dataframes.py:455 from_dta -> pandas/io/stata.py:1698 read); pandas.io.stata.StataReader._read_old_header source shows 'raise ValueError(f"cannot convert stata types ...") from err'; CSV first-byte sweep over countries/*/*/Data/**/*.csv.dvc blobs (93 present / 320 missing / 0 hits).
approach: Sniff, do not widen: in read_file (local_tools.py) only attempt from_dta when the first bytes are a Stata header -- old format: byte0 in 102..115, byte1 in {1,2}, byte2 == 1, byte3 == 0; new format: file starts with b'<stata_dta>' -- and otherwise skip to the next reader. Keep the existing except as-is so a REAL .dta that fails stays loud (a widened bare except would re-create the silent fall-through the repo keeps removing). Same sniff can route .SSP for #699 (magic 'HEADER RECORD*******LIBRARY HEADER RECORD'). Add tests: the hhid_100000 CSV reads via read_csv; a real .dta still reads; a corrupt .dta still raises.
verify: tests/test_local_tools-style unit tests with synthetic files; pytest -n per Makefile recipe on tests touching get_dataframe; cold build of one small YAML-path country (e.g. Albania) to show the sniff changes nothing for real .dta. CACHE COST: any edit to get_dataframe/read_file moves 37/37 _table_cache_hash (Site R rule) -> corpus-wide re-warm; batch with #699 and the #805 reader change so there is one re-warm.

title: _apply_categorical_mappings nulls non-string values via an unguarded .str.strip() on any column whose name matches a categorical table
priority_why: A silent-null tripwire with measured zero exposure today (the issue's own census and nothing since changes it); worth closing because it is a one-line fix with a regression test.
summary: Claim holds verbatim: lsms_library/country.py:3048-3050 still reads `if hasattr(df[col], 'str'): df[col] = df[col].str.strip()` before `.replace(rdict)`, and pd.Series(['U','Urban',None,1,4],dtype=object).str.strip() -> ['U','Urban',None,nan,nan] on pandas 3.0.6. The hazard is COLUMN-only: the index-level branch (country.py:3058-3063) uses df.rename(index=rdict, level=...) with no strip. No regression test exists (no test references the strip). approach: country.py:3049 -> strip only strings: `df[col] = df[col].map(lambda v: v.strip() if isinstance(v, str) else v)` (or a boolean mask over isinstance), then `.replace(rdict)`. title: Panama 1997: 99.1% of u='Value' rows carry Quantity = 7.70, an undecoded missing-value sentinel served as data
priority_why: A served Quantity that is not a measurement in 10,973 rows of food_acquired (and it blocks #770 Step 2 for Panama); it is a wave-script decode defect with the mechanism now identified.
summary: Claim holds on the warm cache with one spelling correction: the rows are u='value' (lowercase, the survey's own unit code 77 'valor' decoded through units.json Translation), not the library's capital 'Value' (46 rows, clean). 1997: 11,026 lowercase-value rows, Quantity 7.7 in 10,973 of them; 7-repunit family 10,979 rows total; only 2 non-value rows carry 7.7. MECHANISM (new, from the raw file): in GAST-A.DTA ga106a == 7.7 on 10,800 rows and 10,798 of them have ga106b == 77; of the 10,847 ga106b == 77 rows, ga106a is 7.7 on 10,798, 77.0 on 3, 6.0 on 2, 1.0 on 1. The 15-day side is identical: ga110a == 7.7 on 175 rows, all 175 with ga110b == 77. So 7.70 co-occurs almost exactly with unit code 77 ('valor'); this is consistent with the unit code echoed into the quantity slot (77 at one implied decimal), not with a free-standing missing sentinel -- an interpretation of the co-occurrence, since the questionnaire was not read. Panama/1997/_/food_acquired.py:60-66 masks only the 9999.x band and never looks at the unit code; ga106c (expenditure) on those rows is real (median 2.70). The questionnaire (pn97hhq.pdf) was not consulted: no pdftotext on this node.
evidence: pd.read_parquet Panama/var/food_acquired.parquet (1997: value 11,026 rows, 7.7 x 10,973; Value 46 rows); get_dataframe('../Data/GAST-A.DTA', convert_categoricals=False) from Panama/1997/_ (cold pull of one blob into the private root): crosstabs above; Panama/_/units.json Unitcode 77 = valor/value, conversion null; Panama/1997/_/food_acquired.py:60-66, 82-83, 118-121; Panama/_/CONTENTS.org:940-978.
approach: Panama/1997/_/food_acquired.py: after decode_unit, for rows with unit code 77 (u == 'value') set Quantity to NA (option A) -- or fold them into the library's value-only convention u='Value', Quantity = Expenditure (option B, which CONTENTS.org:954-962 describes as the convention the script already applies to the capital-Value rows at :169-175). Either way stop serving 7.70; record the unit-77 co-occurrence in Panama/_/CONTENTS.org; keep the 2 stray 7.7 rows in other units untouched (they are not the pattern). Then #770 Step 2 for Panama is unblocked.
verify: Cold build of Country('Panama').food_acquired() in a private root: assert no 1997 row has Quantity == 7.7 with u in {'value','Value'}; Expenditure totals unchanged (sum ga106c < 9999 reconciles as the script asserts); food_quantities(units='kgs') row count unchanged (carry rule). CACHE COST: Panama/1997/_/food_acquired.py is in the binp: glob of every 1997-wave table and so in every Panama L2-country hash -> full Panama re-warm (3 waves, small); no other country.

Also :893-938 ENV-97 is format 104/105 and ga106b is 37.2% the 2^333 missing double. The unit-77-echo mechanism found here is NOT recorded and should be added.
decision_for_human: For the 10,973 unit-code-77 rows: A) serve Quantity = NA and keep u='value' (honest null, rows stay as expenditure-only observations) or B) fold into the library convention u='Value', Quantity = Expenditure?
